In the month of July 2026, 15.98 million subscribers submitted their requests for Mobile Number Portability (MNP). The number of active wireless (mobile) subscribers (on the date of peak VLR # ) in July 2026 was 1204.01 million.
____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Note:
* The wireless subscriber base comprises of wireless mobile telephone subscribers (including M2M cellular mobile connections), and FWA subscribers.
@ Tele-density has been computed on the basis of the projection of population from the ‘Report of the Technical Group on Population Projections for India and States 2011 – 2036’, published in July 2020.
# VLR is an acronym of Visitor Location Register. The dates of peak VLR for various Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) July be different in different service areas.
Information in this press release is based on the data provided by the Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) to TRAI.

enrichment.summary: The release presents TRAI-sourced telecom subscription data for India as of July 2026, showing total telephone subscribers at 1354.28 million with a monthly net addition of 6.20 million (0.46% growth). It details wireless/wireline splits, urban-rural distribution (58.83% urban, 41.17% rural share), tele-density figures (94.68% overall, 154.12% urban, 61.05% rural), broadband subscriber counts, and 15.98 million Mobile Number Portability requests during the month.
enrichment.context: This is a routine monthly statistical bulletin that the Department of Telecommunications releases based on data submitted by Telecom Service Providers to TRAI. Such releases track India's progress on tele-density and the urban-rural digital divide, which are relevant to Digital India goals and universal service obligations funded through the Universal Service Obligation Fund. Persistent gaps between urban (154%) and rural (61%) tele-density reflect ongoing challenges in last-mile rural connectivity, a recurring theme in telecom policy discussions, BharatNet expansion, and spectrum allocation debates. However, these monthly releases are largely repetitive data updates without new policy announcements, making them primarily reference material rather than exam-worthy content.
